Abstract:

Blazars are among the most energetic and variable subclasses of active galactic nuclei (AGN), characterized by relativistic jets oriented close to the observer&rsquos line of sight. Their emission extends across the entire electromagnetic spectrum, from radio to very-high-energy gamma rays, and is dominated by non-thermal radiation processes amplified by relativistic Doppler boosting. Owing to their extreme luminosity, rapid variability, and broad spectral coverage, blazars provide unique laboratories for studying particle acceleration, relativistic jet dynamics, high-energy radiation mechanisms, and the interaction between jets and supermassive black holes. Multiwavelength spectral energy distribution (SED) studies of different blazar subclasses are therefore essential for understanding the physical conditions governing jet formation, evolution, and energy dissipation.

In this work, a detailed multi-wavelength broadband spectral analysis of the blazar OJ 287 is performed using quasi-simultaneous observations spanning the optical/UV, X-ray, and high-energy &gamma-ray bands. OJ 287 is one of the most extensively studied blazars and exhibits strong variability across the electromagnetic spectrum, making it an ideal source for investigating relativistic jet physics. The observed broadband emission is interpreted within a one-zone leptonic framework, where synchrotron radiation and inverse Compton scattering are responsible for the low- and high-energy components of the SED, respectively. The underlying electron energy distribution is modeled using a broken power-law formulation. By fitting the model to the observed data, key jet parameters including the magnetic field strength, emission region size, bulk Lorentz factor, Doppler factor, and electron energy distribution are constrained. The jet energetics are further investigated by estimating the contributions from relativistic electrons, cold protons, magnetic fields, and radiative output. The results indicate a highly energetic, particle-dominated jet and provide important constraints on the physical processes governing broadband emission, particle acceleration, and energy dissipation in blazar jets.
